dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the handover sheet and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The unit roster review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
Standard shifts since I returned have been physically uneventful, wrist included.
The baseline is fully recovered.
Fully, per every checkup.
Someone new shadowed me in the intensive care unit this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the manual handling into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
My wrist rehabilitation finished in the spring: full range, full strength on the final assessment, and six months of normal duties since without a single complaint.
The recovery is documented and complete.
As complete as these things get.
Routine repositioning with the ceiling hoists costs my wrist nothing.
Assisted handling is a non-issue.
A complete non-issue.
I archived last cycle's notes on the unit roster and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The occupational health team offers a graded manual-handling strength assessment, and the next slot is early next month.
A clean measurement is available soon.
Booked, in fact.
A vendor call about the handover sheet ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the intensive care unit checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the manual handling.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the unit roster records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
My single trial shift with the proning team left the wrist sore for two days, but it was also my first week back from leave and my grip conditioning was at its lowest.
One sore sample, badly confounded.
Confounded enough to mean almost nothing.
I sketched next week's plan for the manual handling before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the handover sheet updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The proning team runs scheduled manual turns through every shift; it is the most wrist-loaded rotation in the unit.
The load profile is real regardless.
Real, and worth measuring properly first.
I compared two options for the unit roster tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the intensive care unit handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
The ECMO coordinator wants my decision on joining the proning team. Realistically, how should I respond this week?
